criterion_notes.c1: Examines rural household and village drinking water and sanitation service access in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 (plain=yes -> plain_criterion2_decision='include') because the VEA intervention includes an institutional/governance component ('strengthening of village-level WASH institutions', electing village WASH committees, and Healthy Village certification) and measures a village-level water governance index. Fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading (narrow=no -> decision='exclude', E03) because the exposure evaluated in the RCT is a bundled rural WASH project-delivery package combining direct infrastructure financing/construction, behavioural promotion, and community WASH committee mobilisation rather than a rule-type legal, administrative, tariff, tenure, eligibility, enforcement, or utility-ownership/regulatory mechanism directly governing service access, and the trial cannot disaggregate the institutional component from infrastructure construction and behaviour-change promotion.
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical cluster-randomised controlled trial collecting primary survey data across 121 village clusters (328 surveyed villages, 1,312 households).
criterion_notes.c4: Reports household-level access outcomes including use of an improved primary drinking water source, use of an improved primary sanitation facility, time spent collecting water, water quantity collected, and financial cost of water, plus village-level functional improved water points.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the population and units of analysis (1,312 households and 328 villages grouped into 121 clusters in four rural DRC provinces), exposure (randomised assignment to the multi-component VEA programme), outcomes, and study design (cluster-randomised controlled trial).

evidence_quotes.quote: Primary outcomes included time spent collecting water; quantity of water collected; prevalence of improved primary source of drinking water; and prevalence of improved primary defecation site.

The VEA programme was a comprehensive attempt to address multiple WASH gaps in rural DRC, combining construction and rehabilitation of water infrastructure and sanitation facilities, community mobilisation for behaviour change and support to community WASH institutions.
There is far less ability to disaggregate any distinct mechanism of action in the VEA trial than in the aforementioned studies, which separately tested water, sanitation and nutrition interventions.
We used statistical software (Stata V.16) to randomise the sample into 50 treatment clusters (containing 145 treatment villages) and 71 control clusters (183 control villages).

raw_response.exposure: Assignment at the village-cluster level to the Healthy Villages and Schools (Villages et Ecoles Assainis, VEA) programme, a bundled four-component rural WASH intervention combining water infrastructure construction/rehabilitation, sanitation infrastructure construction/rehabilitation, village WASH committee mobilisation/training, and hygiene behaviour-change promotion.
raw_response.outcome: Primary outcomes (household level): time spent collecting water, quantity of water collected, improved primary drinking water source, and improved primary sanitation facility; secondary outcomes include financial cost of water, water satisfaction, handwashing/sanitation/water storage practices, child health, school attendance (household/child level), and functional water points and water governance index (village level).
raw_response.population_and_sample: 1,312 rural households and village/WASH leaders across 328 surveyed villages grouped into 121 clusters (50 treatment clusters, 71 control clusters) in four provinces (Kongo Central, Kasai, Kasai Central, South Kivu) of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification. Although the study is a rigorous cluster-randomised controlled trial measuring household water and sanitation access outcomes and passes the literal/plain wording of Criterion 2 because the bundled VEA intervention includes village WASH committee formation and measures a local water governance index, the tested exposure is a multi-component WASH project-delivery package (infrastructure subsidies/construction, hygiene behaviour-change promotion, and community mobilisation) whose components are not disaggregated. It does not evaluate a rule-type legal, administrative, regulatory, tariff, eligibility, documentation/tenure, enforcement, or utility-ownership mechanism directly governing service access.
raw_response.study_design: Cluster-randomised controlled trial (intention-to-treat linear regression analysis)
